newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile to offer plan on Mercosur-FTAA integration.
newsitem.headline: Chile to offer plan on Mercosur-FTAA integration.

text.p: Chile this week will present a summit of leaders from the Mercosur trade bloc with a concrete plan for integrating the South American group with a proposed hemispheric free-trade zone, President Eduardo Frei said Wednesday.

Frei said Chile's proposal would seek to create a consensus among Mercosur members on integrating the bloc with the Free Trade Area of the Americas (FTAA), which the Clinton administration wants to create by the year 2005, and with the European Union.

"Tomorrow we are going to make a very concrete proposal on the issue of integration between Mercosur and the European Union, and Mercosur and ALCA," Frei reporters before leaving for the summit in Paraguay. ALCA is the FTAA acronym in Spanish.

The Mercosur bloc's four full members -- Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay -- have said they want to move slowly and cautiously on integration with FTAA, while Washington wants to speed up efforts.
Chile, an associate member of Mercosur with sometimes prickly relations with the bloc, has said it prefers to strengthen the FTAA rather than stress growth of Mercosur.

Frei said the Mersocur leaders would seek a common approach to trade issues before the second Summit of the Americas in the Chilean capital of Santiago next March, at which talks for a FTAA are to get under way.
The United States envisions the FTAA building on the North American Free Trade Agreement, now linking the United States, Canada and Mexico, to extend to the rest of the hemisphere.
"We're looking for a common Mercosur position before the Summit of the Americas in Chile next year," he said.
